#: Command line: help, column headings, messages and refusals.
cli.cmd.binding: which bones own what the morph moves
cli.cmd.bones: bones and how many vertices each holds
cli.cmd.bounds: bounding spheres of the shapes: in the file, the one needed, the walk
cli.cmd.budget: amplitude budget: at what value each slider crosses the threshold
cli.cmd.catalog: a catalogue of meshes under a folder
cli.cmd.chains: bone chains for swinging physics: skin along the links
cli.cmd.env: whether we run under MO2 and what the browse root is
cli.cmd.fit: fit capsules to the skin at the current sliders
cli.cmd.focus: aim the camera: at a bone, a morph or a shape
cli.cmd.layers: whether the covers follow the skin
cli.cmd.missing: which expected sliders are not in the file
cli.cmd.physics: settings of one swinging engine: smp (XML) or cbpc (lines of three files)
cli.cmd.serve: a page with the list of meshes on a local port
cli.cmd.strain: where a morph tears the surface
cli.cmd.web: a self-contained page with the viewer
cli.col.name: name
cli.err.assignPair: --assign: expected <stem substring>=smp|cbpc separated by commas, not %(value)r
cli.err.clearanceNeedsMesh: --clearance measures capsules against skin: name a mesh as well
cli.err.collidersNoSkeleton: --colliders without a skeleton: there is no %(file)s next to the mesh, add --skeleton <skeleton.nif>
cli.err.noMesh: name a mesh: a path to a .nif, or --entry <number|name> [--root folder]
cli.err.notNumbers: %(key)s: expected numbers separated by commas, not %(value)r
cli.err.nothingToStop: at %(url)s: %(state)s - there is nothing to stop
cli.msg.bonesMoved: bones whose vertices the morph moves:
cli.msg.bonesPartly: bones moved only partly - this is where the surface stretches:
cli.msg.checkClean: %(file)s: refers only to what the skeleton%(andMesh)s actually has
cli.opt.binding.shape: shape of the mesh; baseShape from the settings by default
cli.opt.bounds.margin: margin over the needed radius as a share; boundsMargin by default
cli.opt.bounds.shape: one shape; all of them by default
cli.opt.bounds.shrink: when writing, shrink spheres to the needed size as well; without it a sphere only grows
cli.opt.bounds.write: write the corrected spheres into a NEW file
cli.opt.budget.threshold: strain threshold; strainThreshold from the settings by default
cli.opt.catalog.all: meshes without a morph file as well
cli.opt.catalog.root: browse root; without it - the game Data under MO2, or catalogRoot from the settings
cli.opt.chains.assign: who a chain is given to for this run, over the settings: tail=smp,ear=cbpc
cli.opt.chains.engine: only chains given to this engine (chainEngines in the settings)
cli.opt.chains.only: which shapes of the mesh to count
cli.opt.colliders.clearance: and how they sit against the skin at the current sliders
cli.opt.fit.bundle: a bundle of N capsules instead of one: the cloud is cut into pieces
cli.opt.fit.percentile: share of points inside the radius; from the settings by default
cli.opt.fit.ppb: print the settings lines for Precision Physic Bodies
cli.opt.fit.split: how to cut: slices along the bone axis or clusters; bundleSplit by default
cli.opt.focus.bone: a bone name or a part of one
cli.opt.layers.adjacent: only covers lying over moved skin - the ones that must follow
cli.opt.layers.base: base shape; baseShape from the settings by default
cli.opt.physics.assign: who a chain is given to for this run, over the settings: tail=smp,ear=cbpc
cli.opt.physics.check: check a ready settings file of this engine: does it refer to bones of the skeleton and shapes of the mesh; exit code 3 if there are findings
cli.opt.physics.engine: which engine: chains of the other one are left out
cli.opt.physics.only: which shapes of the mesh count as skin
cli.opt.physics.out: write the text to a file; without it, print
cli.opt.physics.percentile: share of points inside the capsule radius; from the settings by default
cli.opt.serve.all: meshes without a morph file as well
cli.opt.serve.host: address; serveHost from the settings by default
cli.opt.serve.parent: number of the process the server leaves with; without it there is no watch
cli.opt.serve.port: port; servePort from the settings by default
cli.opt.serve.root: browse root; the same default as catalog
cli.opt.serve.status: whether a server is up at this address
cli.opt.strain.by: order of pairs: max - by strain together, gain - by what the pair adds over the worse of the two alone
cli.opt.strain.pairs: walk every pair of sliders at --amount: which two together tear worse than either alone
cli.opt.strain.slider: slider value NAME=NUMBER, repeatable: strain under a SET of sliders (--morph and --amount do not apply then)
cli.opt.strain.threshold: strain threshold; strainThreshold from the settings by default
cli.opt.strain.top: how many of the worst pairs to show; 0 - all of them
cli.opt.top.skeleton: skeleton file: the collision capsules are read from it
cli.opt.view.bumper: and the movement cylinder: it is four times the size of the body
cli.opt.view.colliders: a layer of capsules over the body; needs --skeleton
cli.opt.view.entry: a mesh from the catalogue by number or name instead of a path to a .nif
cli.opt.view.light: light behind the camera (camera) or apart from it (world)
cli.opt.view.lightdir: direction to the source x,y,z: in camera axes under --light camera, otherwise in world axes (--light-dir=0.3,0.5,0.8)
cli.opt.view.look: an arbitrary view: turn,lift in degrees (with a minus: --look=-10,5)
cli.opt.view.pan: shift the frame right,up in model units (with a minus: --pan=-5,3)
cli.opt.view.zoomat: zoom to a point: new zoom,x,y - the point as shares of half the shorter side of the frame from the centre, right and up (--zoom-at=2,0.4,-0.3)
cli.serve.rootOnPage: not set - name a folder on the page
cli.state.busy: the port is taken by another program
cli.state.slow: someone is there but does not answer
cli.status.here: this process under MO2: %(yes)s;  game Data: %(data)s
cli.usage:
morphbench - a workbench for body morphs, outside the game.

    python mb.py summary <mesh.nif>
    python mb.py shapes  <mesh.nif>
    python mb.py bones   <mesh.nif> [--shape body] [--find Hand]
    python mb.py morphs  <mesh.nif> [--morph Paw] [--shape body]
    python mb.py empty   <mesh.nif>
    python mb.py missing <mesh.nif> CLAWNeck CLAWEars ...
    python mb.py strain  <mesh.nif> [--morph Paw] [--threshold 0.25] [--amount 1.0]
    python mb.py strain  <mesh.nif> --slider A=1 --slider B=1     strain under a SET of sliders
    python mb.py strain  <mesh.nif> --pairs [--top 10] [--by gain]  every pair: which two tear together
    python mb.py budget  <mesh.nif> [--threshold 0.25]            at what value each slider tears
    python mb.py layers  <mesh.nif> --morph CLAWBelly [--base body] [--adjacent]
    python mb.py binding <mesh.nif> --shape body --morph CLAWPawSize
    python mb.py focus   <mesh.nif> [--bone Finger | --morph CLAWPawSize | --shape head]
    python mb.py render  <mesh.nif> --out frame.png [--view front | --look 40,15] [--colour bone]
                         [--slider CLAWEars=1] [--only body,head] [--morph CLAWPawSize]
                         [--focus-bone Finger | --focus-morph CLAWPawSize | --focus-shape head]
                         [--zoom 2 | --zoom-at=2,0.4,-0.3] [--pan=5,-3] [--size 900x900]
                         [--light camera|world] [--light-dir=x,y,z] [--light-power=a,d,f]
    python mb.py bounds  <mesh.nif> [--shape S] [--write new.nif]   bounding spheres: in the file, needed, the walk
    python mb.py chains  <mesh.nif> [--skeleton S.nif] [--engine smp|cbpc] [--assign tail=smp,ear=cbpc]
                                                       bone chains: skin along links, breaks, who they are given to
    python mb.py physics <mesh.nif> [--skeleton S.nif] --engine smp|cbpc [--assign ...] [--out file]
    python mb.py physics <mesh.nif> [--skeleton S.nif] --engine smp|cbpc --check <ready file>
                                                       settings of one swinging engine in its own format
    python mb.py colliders [mesh.nif] --skeleton <skeleton.nif> [--find Thigh] [--clearance]
    python mb.py fit       <mesh.nif> --skeleton <skeleton.nif> [--find Thigh] [--slider X=1]
                           [--only body] [--bundle N --split axis|kmeans] [--save new.nif] [--ppb]
    python mb.py sheet   <mesh.nif> --out folder [--views front,side,below] [--prefix view]
    python mb.py web     <mesh.nif> --out page.html  (the same keys as render)
    python mb.py env                                   whether we run under MO2 and what the browse root is
    python mb.py catalog [folder] [--all] [--find X]   meshes under a folder with their morph files
    python mb.py serve   [--root folder] [--port N] [--nif X]   page with the list of meshes
    python mb.py serve   --status | --stop             is a server up; stop it

`serve` with no keys simply brings a server up: the browse root is the game Data under MO2,
otherwise it is named on the page. If a server is already up at that address, a second one
is not started: it is handed the root (under MO2 - the game Data this process sees) and the
page is opened. The window `morphbench.exe` next to it does the same with buttons - start,
stop, state, browse folder, page - and under MO2 it sees Data with every mod of the build.

For render, sheet and web a mesh can be taken from the catalogue instead of a path:
`--entry <number|name> [--root folder]`. The skeleton (`skeleton.nif` next to the mesh) is
picked up by itself, otherwise `--skeleton` works with any command; render, sheet and web
understand `--colliders` - a layer of capsules over the body.
Every command takes `--json`: the same answer machine-readable, without tables.
The morph file is picked up next to the mesh; `--tri` names it explicitly.
Pairs of numbers starting with a minus are written with an equals sign: `--pan=-5,3`.
